narrative.overview:
Technicat Automation looks and behaves like an engineer's marked-up review surface: cool drafting-white workplanes, graphite rules, dense schedules, and compact controls. The visual hierarchy favors evidence, editable quantities, conflicts, and sign-off state over decoration. Technical blue identifies the current task and primary action; amber marks unresolved decisions; green appears only after explicit approval.

The interface is an Operate-mode Windows desktop tool. Familiar Qt navigation, persistent context rails, dense tables, and explicit pricing gates carry the experience. The system is planar and structural: depth comes from adjacent tones and one-pixel rules, not floating-card shadows. State changes are immediate, with no authored decorative animation.
keyCharacteristics: Drafting-white work surfaces bounded by cool-gray and graphite rules.
Dense, scan-first tables with compact labels and persistent engineering context.
Technical blue reserved for selection, focus, the active workflow stage, and primary actions.
Amber, green, and exclusion gray paired with explicit text or decision labels.
Square-to-gently-curved geometry, mostly two- and three-pixel radii.
Segoe UI for the workbench; Cascadia Mono or Consolas for IDs, evidence, measurements, and logs.

rules.name: The One Technical Voice Rule
rules.body: Technical blue identifies interaction and current position; it is not decorative fill.

rules.name: The Decision Color Rule
rules.body: Green means approved, amber means unresolved, gray means excluded, and every use is reinforced by text, a decision column, or a status label.

rules.name: The Evidence Type Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for identifiers, measurements, evidence, and logs; prose and controls stay in Segoe UI.

rules.name: The Three-Plane Review Rule
rules.body: Panel context stays left, the active schedule stays central, and evidence plus decision actions stay right.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Add depth with tonal separation and rules; do not introduce floating-card shadows, glass, blur, or gradient elevation.

rules.name: The Drafting Edge Rule
rules.body: Reusable controls stay within the implemented 2-3px corner vocabulary; rounded capsules and oversized squircles do not belong in the workbench.

dos: Do keep evidence, conflicts, confidence, manufacturer, and the explicit decision adjacent in review flows.
Do use dense ruled tables for schedules and editable engineering data.
Do reserve technical blue for current position, focus, selection, and primary action.
Do pair every approval, warning, exclusion, error, and blocked state with words or another non-color cue.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, native tab order, shortcuts, and Qt scaling behavior.
Do keep pricing visibly locked until the review gate passes.
donts: Don't introduce floating-card shadows, glassmorphism, gradients, decorative blobs, or soft SaaS-style visual effects.
Don't replace the desktop workbench with generic metric-card dashboards or a console-first workflow.
Don't use green for generic success decoration or amber for neutral emphasis; these colors carry decision meaning.
Don't hide dense engineering data behind hover-only affordances or color-only status.
Don't add decorative motion; preserve the immediate state-change model and reduced-motion safety.
Don't round controls into pills or expand the established 2-3px radius vocabulary without a functional reason.
